message.content: In lions, the presence of a mane is a classic example of a dominant genetic trait. Male lions inherit the allele that promotes mane growth from either parent, and the trait is expressed regardless of whether the other allele is present. This dominant allele leads to the development of the mane during puberty, driven by testosterone levels.
